events.body: The panels aren't right for the room. I'd like to send them back. Please get a return set up quickly, I need the hallway clear by the weekend. If I have to pay the carriage to get it moving, fine, I'll pay it.
Return RA-6788 authorised for TG-8030, 14 cartons. Reason code: change of mind. Under that code the customer pays return carriage; 96.00 will be deducted from the refund.
Labels issued for RA-6788. Return shipment DL-9067, Copperhythe Arc collection 2 October.
RA-6788 received at the warehouse, 14 cartons, unopened bar one. Passed to Refunds team.
TG-8030 refunded today less 96.00 return carriage as per reason code. Return closed.

I've seen the refund. I should have been clearer at the start and I'm correcting that now: I did not change my mind. The listing describes the panels as 'white, satin finish'. What arrived was off-white, matt and rough to the touch. I've uploaded a screenshot of the listing and four photographs to the order. I only said I'd pay the carriage because I needed them out of the hall. I'm asking for the return reason to be looked at again.
TG-8030: the customer says the goods were not as described and asks for the return reason to be reviewed. He has uploaded evidence to the order.
TG-8030: reason code can't be changed once the refund has been issued. Refund is out, return is closed.

Correction to yesterday's work-queue reply on TG-8030, which was wrong. A reason code can be reviewed for 30 days after the refund where the customer gives evidence that the item differed from its listing. We can see his uploads on the order. A review only starts on a written request to this team by Email that quotes the return number and states the specific differences claimed; the work-queue note did neither. Who bears the return carriage follows from the outcome and is for us and Refunds team to decide.

The return page now reads 'closed, change of mind', and I gather the position was that nothing can be altered once a refund has gone out. I don't accept that. A refund having been paid doesn't change what the listing said. To be exact about it: the listing says white; these were off-white. It says satin finish; these were matt. And they were rough to the touch, which nobody would take 'satin' to mean. Colour, finish, texture. I'm not asking for a favour. I'm asking for the reason to be recorded correctly and for the 96.00 to follow from that. Please tell me what happens next.

My sister's a solicitor and she just laughed when I told her about this saga.
